Create segment persona cards as a gt table

Source: R/profiling.R
create_persona_table.Rd

Generates a publication-ready "This / Not That" table showing the defining characteristics of each discovered segment. Over-indexed attributes (index= 120) are listed as "More Likely", under-indexed (index <= 80) as "Less Likely".

Usage

create_persona_table(profile_result, cluster_profile = NULL)

Arguments

profile_result

Result from jtbd_profile_segments()

cluster_profile

Optional result from jtbd_cluster_profile() to include top opportunity scores in the persona

Value

A gt table object

See also

Other clustering: jtbd_cluster(), jtbd_cluster_profile(), jtbd_feature_matrix(), jtbd_find_k(), jtbd_pca(), jtbd_profile_segments(), jtbd_segment(), plot_cluster_heatmap(), plot_elbow(), plot_pca_biplot(), plot_pca_loadings(), plot_pca_scree(), plot_segment_dna(), plot_segment_fingerprint(), plot_segment_index(), plot_segment_profiles(), plot_segment_radar(), plot_segment_radar_facet()

Examples

data(jtbd_sample)
cl <- jtbd_cluster(jtbd_sample, n_clusters = 3)
#> Feature matrix: 200 respondents x 12 objectives (opportunity scores 1-9).
#> Kaiser rule: retaining 5 components (eigenvalue > 1).
#> ✔ Clustered 200 respondents into 3 segments.
#> ℹ Sizes: Segment_1 (n=60), Segment_2 (n=76), Segment_3 (n=64)
prof <- jtbd_profile_segments(cl$data)
#> ✔ Profiled 6 variables across 3 segments.
#> ℹ 2 variables significantly distinguish segments (p < 0.05).
#> ℹ Top distinguisher: segment, income
opp_profile <- jtbd_cluster_profile(jtbd_sample, cl, test_sig = FALSE)
#> Found 3 segments with n > 30.
create_persona_table(prof, opp_profile)
